founderLine: Your model router can pick a model with a small decision model instead of starting a full agent for each routed message, and today's agent stays as the fallback.
whyItFits: classifyWithLLM() starts a headless agent with the router's fallback model, and that agent's only job is to call select_category with one category from a fixed list. This is the job decision models were built for: one answer from a fixed list, with a probability for each option.
risks: Routing moves to a different provider, so each classified message goes to OpenAI even when the router's fallback is another provider, and the answer is probabilistic. The setting is off by default. When it's on, classifyWithLLM() is unchanged and still answers when the chosen category's probability is under 0.70, when the call fails or is refused, when the API returns a category it wasn't offered, or when there is no OPEN_AI_KEY. A "none" at 0.70 or above is final and means no rule matched; a "none" under 0.70 goes to the agent, because a weak "none" can hide a rule that should have matched. From the 22 Oct update, a long category list is cached: a write costs 1.25 times normal input and lasts at least 30 minutes, so a router that gets less than about one message every 30 minutes can pay that rate on each message instead of getting a discount.
rollback: Set ROUTER_CLASSIFIER=agent, or remove the setting.

vendor.claim: typed answers 10x faster than the Responses API

stages.whatShipped: The Decisions API became generally available on 22 Oct, adding prompt caching on shared input, input_json and more questions per request.
stages.whatThisChanges: Only server/utils/agents/aibitat/plugins/router-classifier.js and its test. A category list that looks long enough for the API's 1,024-token minimum moves into a shared prefix in input, with an explicit cache breakpoint before the user's message, because content in questions can't be cached. Length is judged from the list's size in bytes, so no tokenizer runs over the list, and a list near the minimum can land on either side of it, which only costs a missed discount. A shorter list keeps its plain choices with caching turned off, and gets no cache discount, and that includes the list in this fork's test set. Caching is turned off there because the API would otherwise write a long user message to the cache at the write rate. A cache write costs 1.25 times normal input and lasts at least 30 minutes, so a long list on a router that gets less than about one message every 30 minutes can pay that rate on each message instead of getting a discount. On a long list the descriptions leave the choices and the same 0.70 threshold applies, so it's a different request from the one the lab's table measures. The table only measures the short form, and the lab's separate long-list check, once it has run, covers the test set's rules padded with neutral text, with its messages sent back to back, so its cache reads are the best case and a router with a long list should check its own labelled examples before relying on this. input_json isn't used: the message is plain text, and JSON parts can't carry a breakpoint. The default stays agent.
stages.comment: Updated 22 Oct: Decisions API is generally available.
